<div class="site-page">
  <section class="inner-banner"><div class="inner-shell"><span class="eyebrow">Our research</span><h1>Questions at the edge of particle physics.</h1><p>What are neutrinos? Why does the universe contain matter? How do we build detectors capable of seeing extraordinarily rare events?</p></div></section>
  <section class="section-shell" aria-labelledby="research-core"><span class="section-kicker">Current major programs</span><h2 id="research-core" class="section-title">Four interconnected experiments.</h2><p class="section-lede">Our group combines detector development, calibration, background modeling, statistics, and machine learning in major international neutrino experiments.</p>

    <article class="research-feature" id="kamland2-zen"><div class="num">01 <span>2024–present</span><div class="feature-art" aria-hidden="true"></div></div><div><h2>KamLAND2-Zen</h2><div class="meta">Next-generation neutrinoless double-beta decay</div><p>KamLAND2-Zen is upgrading the KamLAND detector to improve sensitivity to neutrinoless double-beta decay. The experiment will use a brighter liquid scintillator, improved photomultiplier light collection, and next-generation readout electronics.</p><p>As U.S. spokesperson, Christopher Grant coordinates the U.S. construction effort. Our group leads work on RFSoC-based front-end electronics and detector calibration systems, including their development, installation, and commissioning.</p><a class="text-link" href="https://www.kamland.awa.tohoku.ac.jp/">KamLAND project information <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></div></article>

    <article class="research-feature" id="kamland-zen"><div class="num">02 <span>2019–present</span><div class="feature-art kamland" aria-hidden="true"></div></div><div><h2>KamLAND-Zen</h2><div class="meta">Are neutrinos their own antiparticles?</div><p>KamLAND-Zen searches for neutrinoless double-beta decay of xenon-136. Observing this process would show that lepton number is not conserved and provide compelling evidence that neutrinos have a Majorana mass.</p><p>Grant has served as U.S. spokesperson since 2023 and leads U.S. data-analysis efforts. Our group established a Bayesian analysis framework and co-developed KamNet, a spatiotemporal neural network for distinguishing rare signals from backgrounds. We contributed to the 2023 and 2025 major KamLAND-Zen results.</p><a class="text-link" href="https://doi.org/10.1103/jkf6-48j8">Complete-dataset KamLAND-Zen result <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></div></article>

    <article class="research-feature" id="cupid"><div class="num">03 <span>2021–present</span><div class="feature-art cupid" aria-hidden="true"></div></div><div><h2>CUPID</h2><div class="meta">Cryogenic detectors for rare decays</div><p>CUPID is developing an ultra-low-background cryogenic experiment to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay in molybdenum-100. Its scintillating bolometers simultaneously measure particle-induced heat and light.</p><p>Our contributions include advanced readout and machine-learning techniques, radioactive material screening, and studies of cosmogenic activation in molybdenum. Grant serves on the CUPID Experiment Council.</p><a class="text-link" href="https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-025-14352-1">CUPID overview paper <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></div></article>

    <article class="research-feature" id="eos"><div class="num">04 <span>2021–present</span><div class="feature-art eos" aria-hidden="true"></div></div><div><h2>Eos</h2><div class="meta">Seeing with scintillation and Cherenkov light</div><p>Eos is a demonstrator for hybrid optical detection that combines the timing and directional information of Cherenkov light with the higher light yield of scintillation. This approach may enable future neutrino detectors to reconstruct both energy and direction with improved precision.</p><p>Our group developed self-triggering beta calibration sources, contributes to calibration and background analysis, and investigates sensitivity to sterile-neutrino and dark-sector signatures for a proposed deployment at the Spallation Neutron Source.</p><a class="text-link" href="https://doi.org/10.1103/7qkt-mnqz">Eos detector performance paper <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></div></article>
